Fixed. Two distinct stow 2.4.1 --dotfiles bugs, both rooted in --dotfiles name translation applied to a *directory*:

1. Fold bug (the one reported). Folded ~/.agents -> dot-agents, stow re-appends the translated name when it needs to unfold and looks for the nonexistent dot-agents/.agents.
2. Descend bug (only visible once #1 was cleared). Unfolded, stow descends into dot-agents/skills — a symlink to a directory — and mangles the path again: 'cannot read directory: dev/personal/dotfiles/.agents/dot-agents/skills'.

Either aborts with exit 2 before linking anything, making install.sh a total no-op.

Fix (install.sh + .stow-local-ignore):
- mkdir -p $HOME/.agents before stow, same guard ~/.warp already had — kills #1 by preventing the fold.
- Ignore ^/\.agents/skills$ and have install.sh ln -sfn it after stow — kills #2.

Key finding worth keeping: a *top-level* package entry cannot be ignored at all. ^/\.agents$, ^/\.agents, ^/dot-agents and \.agents were all tested and all still conflicted, while ^/\.codex (same form) works and ^/install\.sh$ works — so ^/-anchored patterns are fine in general, just not for the entry stow is currently placing at level 0. Nested paths like ^/\.agents/skills$ do match, and against the *translated* name (.agents, not dot-agents). That's why the fix skips one child rather than excluding dot-agents wholesale.

Also cleared en route: six real files (orca-agent-status/orca-prefill/orca-titlebar-spinner .ts under ~/.omp and ~/.pi/agent/extensions) blocking stow — verified byte-identical to their repo copies, deleted, now linked. And a stray 1.4MB Mach-O the 1Password installer had dropped over the ~/.local/bin/op-ssh-sign symlink; the repo shim (which execs the app-bundle binary) is back and commit signing verified good.
